# 🗓️ Brisbane Events This Week: 11–17 May 2026

Here is every relevant in-person event I found across Eventbrite, Meetup, Humanitix, QAGOMA, BCC, UQ Science, Must Do Brisbane, Broadsheet, The Urban List, and Visit Brisbane. All events have been filtered to match your interests and skip criteria.

---

## 🧠 PUBLIC LECTURES & TALKS

---

### 1. 🌾 BrisScience: "The Heat Is On – Growing Food in a Warmer World"
- **Date & Time:** Monday 11 May, 6:30–7:30pm
- **Venue:** The Edge, State Library of Queensland, South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Free (registration on Eventbrite)
- **Category:** Public Lecture
- **Source:** science.uq.edu.au / meetup.com/gentle-thinkers
- **URL:** https://www.eventbrite.com.au (search "BrisScience 11 May") / https://science.uq.edu.au/event/brisscience

On 11 May 2026, 6:30–7:30pm, UQ's monthly BrisScience lecture features Dr Millicent Smith exploring how in a warming world we may still be able to grow enough food to feed everyone. BrisScience is a monthly lecture series that brings science out of the labs and to the people, making it accessible to all — run by The University of Queensland. Dr Smith reveals how we can harness novel diversity by screening thousands of plants using cutting-edge phenotyping tools; she is a Senior Lecturer in Crop Physiology at UQ, specialising in climate adaptation in grain legume crops. BrisScience events are held at The Edge, State Library of Queensland, South Brisbane — a visionary space for creatives and innovators, providing resources to explore creativity across art, science, technology, and enterprise.

> 💡 *Perfect for: science enthusiasts, curious generalists, intellectual community seekers. The Gentle Thinkers Meetup group also lists this as a recommended event for their members.*

### 2. 📖 Narelle Oliver Lecture 2026 (Book Links StoryArts Brisbane)
- **Date & Time:** Monday 11 May, 6:00–8:00pm
- **Venue:** St Aidan's Anglican Girls' School, Corinda
- **Cost:** Check Humanitix for ticket price
- **Category:** Public Lecture
- **Source:** events.humanitix.com
- **URL:** https://events.humanitix.com/book-links-storyarts-brisbane

The Narelle Oliver Lecture 2026 takes place Mon 11 May, 6pm–8pm AEST at St Aidan's Anglican Girls' School, Corinda, hosted by Book Links. Book Links is a volunteer-run, not-for-profit organisation in Queensland dedicated to fostering literacy and a love for stories in children and young people — connecting people with stories, authors, and events.

> 💡 *Great for: writers, illustrators, educators, and lovers of children's literature and storytelling culture.*

## 🎭 ARTS / EXHIBITIONS (Ongoing This Week)

---

### 3. 🌈 Olafur Eliasson: Presence — Exhibition at GOMA
- **Date:** Open daily (runs 6 Dec 2025 – 12 July 2026); **GOMA Friday Nights** this week: **Friday 15 May**, from ~5pm–8:30pm
- **Venue:** Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA), South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Exhibition ticketed; Friday Nights component is free entry with exhibition ticket
- **Category:** Arts / Exhibition
- **Source:** qagoma.qld.gov.au / mustdobrisbane.com / visit.brisbane.qld.au
- **URL:** https://www.qagoma.qld.gov.au/event/goma-friday-nights-presence-2026-05-08 / https://www.qagoma.qld.gov.au/stories/olafur-eliasson-presence-in-brisbane

An expansive exhibition by Icelandic-Danish artist Olafur Eliasson featuring major new installations, photography, and sculpture at GOMA — exclusive to Brisbane, developed in close collaboration with the artist and his multidisciplinary Berlin-based studio, spanning the entire ground floor. The exhibition highlights the power of perception and how our senses give shape to our experience of the world — from the seminal 1993 work *Beauty*, which suspends a rainbow in a veil of fine mist, to the immersive rocky landscape of *Riverbed* 2014.

**For GOMA Friday Nights specifically this week:** GOMA is open every Friday night from 1 May until 26 June during *Olafur Eliasson: Presence*. Step into the multi-sensory art of Olafur Eliasson and meet up with sips on a drink and enjoy casual bites — unwind by the river and listen to tunes chosen by cutting-edge DJs, inspired by *Presence*. GOMA Friday Nights runs every Friday night throughout May and June; beyond the exhibition, expect Brisbane's best DJs, captivating pop-up performances, bespoke bars and delicious bites to fuel the night.

> 💡 *One of the most intellectually alive and atmospheric events in Brisbane right now. Ideal for curious, creative, design-minded people.*

### 4. 🏳️‍🌈 "Make A Scene" — Free Exhibition at Queensland Museum Kurilpa
- **Dates:** Until 19 July 2026 (open this week)
- **Venue:** Queensland Museum Kurilpa, South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Free
- **Category:** Arts / Exhibition
- **Source:** theurbanlist.com / visit.brisbane.qld.au
- **URL:** https://www.museum.qld.gov.au/kurilpa

Queensland Museum's free exhibition *Make A Scene* takes you back to an iconic era of Australian queer culture — the fashion-forward 90s showcase features colour, camp, pop culture and community, from fearless self-expressions of LGBTQIA+ identity to the Brisbane-based labels that defined the era. Coinciding with the 35th anniversary of the decriminalisation of homosexuality, the immersive exhibition lets you engage with personal stories from the underground nightclub and dance party scene.

> 💡 *Free, immersive, historically rich, culturally significant. Ideal for people interested in design history, subculture, identity and community.*

## 🎪 ANYWHERE FESTIVAL — WEEK 3 (11–17 May)

The Anywhere Festival's Week 3 runs exactly this week across dozens of unexpected Brisbane venues.

---

### 6. 🎪 Brisbane Anywhere Festival — Week 3 (Multiple Shows)
- **Date:** Monday 11 May – Sunday 17 May 2026
- **Venue:** Venues across Brisbane (Albion, Yeronga, Grange, Milton, CBD, West End, New Farm, Northshore, Kelvin Grove, Fortitude Valley, Paddington, South Brisbane, and more)
- **Cost:** Varies by show (many are low-cost or pay-what-you-can)
- **Category:** Arts / Exhibition / Concert / Community
- **Source:** anywhere.is / mustdobrisbane.com / visit.brisbane.qld.au
- **URL:** https://anywhere.is/brisbane/

The Anywhere Festival runs Week 3 from 11–17 May as part of the month-long festival. A festival where Brisbane's hidden backyards, ferries, lighthouses, driveways and unexpected corners become the stage — since 2011, Anywhere Festival has championed artists by offering rent-free, non-traditional spaces; audiences can stumble upon theatre in hedge mazes, circus in driveways, music in backyards, storytelling on ferries and even musicals in airplanes. Highlights include an extravagant immersive experience at Northshore, a drop-in Self Care Cafe, the story of Gilgamesh projected through smoke, and Matilda Award winner Indiah Morris's immersive show about a Tupperware party — *Airtight*. Back from an epic 92-performance run at Edinburgh Fringe Festival, KMak and Angel Strings return to the planetarium at Mt Coot-tha for a spectacular feast of music as you sit back and explore the universe.

> 💡 *Hundreds of shows across the city this week. Browse the full program at anywhere.is/brisbane/ to find individual show times, venues, and tickets. Perfect for adventurous, arts-curious people.*

## 🎶 CONCERTS & LIVE MUSIC

### 7. 🎷 Bands in Parks: Twilight Jazz by the River
- **Date & Time:** Friday 15 May, 5:00–7:00pm
- **Venue:** Queensland Maritime Museum Park (enter via Dock Street), South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Free (bookings required via Eventbrite)
- **Category:** Concert / Music
- **Source:** eventbrite.com.au / brisbane.qld.gov.au
- **URL:** https://www.eventbrite.com.au/e/bands-in-parks-twilight-jazz-by-the-river-tickets-1982143891738

Bands in Parks: Twilight Jazz by the River takes place Friday May 15, 2026 at Queensland Maritime Museum Park, South Brisbane, presented by Brisbane City Council. Kick back and watch the sunset over the Brisbane River from this beautiful vantage point near the Goodwill Bridge — before the city warms up to Friday evening, take time to enjoy big band jazz after work with the fabulous UQ Big Band.

> 💡 *Free, outdoors, atmospheric, social. Ideal for winding down Friday with strangers who love live music.*

### 8. 🎭 MJ The Musical — Brisbane Season (Ongoing This Week)
- **Date:** Until 24 May (performances Tue–Sun throughout the week)
- **Venue:** Lyric Theatre, QPAC, South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Ticketed (various prices)
- **Category:** Concert / Music / Performing Arts
- **Source:** theurbanlist.com / mustdobrisbane.com
- **URL:** https://www.qpac.com.au

The Olivier and four-time Tony Award-winning musical *MJ The Musical* has thrilled more than 5 million audience members worldwide and is at QPAC's Lyric Theatre — set in 1992, the show offers a behind-the-scenes look into the creation of Michael Jackson's iconic Dangerous World Tour through the lens of an MTV journalist.

> 💡 *Big-budget but genuinely spectacular live performance experience.*

### 9. 🎤 Brisbane Comedy Festival — Ongoing Shows This Week
- **Dates:** Running 24 April – 24 May (shows all week, 11–17 May)
- **Venue:** Brisbane Powerhouse (New Farm), The Tivoli, Fortitude Music Hall, The Princess Theatre (Woolloongabba)
- **Cost:** Ticketed (varies by show)
- **Category:** Concert / Music / Community
- **Source:** mustdobrisbane.com
- **URL:** https://www.brisbanecomedyfestival.com.au

Brisbane Comedy Festival runs from April 24 to May 24, taking over Brisbane Powerhouse, The Tivoli, Fortitude Music Hall and The Princess Theatre — delivering a city-wide comedy takeover for its biggest season yet. Fresh off a record-breaking year, the 2026 festival features bold solo shows, late-night chaos and genre-bending performances, from salacious satire and outrageous silliness to big-hearted storytelling.

> 💡 *Dozens of individual shows to choose from this week — check the program for intimate solo shows at smaller venues like Brisbane Powerhouse. Great for meeting thoughtful, funny people.*

### 10. 🎹 The Drover's Wife – The Opera (World Premiere)
- **Dates:** Running through May at QPAC (check specific dates this week)
- **Venue:** Glasshouse Theatre, QPAC, South Brisbane
- **Cost:** Ticketed
- **Category:** Concert / Music / Performing Arts
- **Source:** mustdobrisbane.com / broadsheet.com.au
- **URL:** https://www.qpac.com.au

The Drover's Wife – The Opera is having its world premiere in QPAC's stunning new Glasshouse Theatre this May. An Australian-themed original opera based on the iconic Henry Lawson short story — rare, thought-provoking and unmissable for those interested in culture and storytelling.

> 💡 *World premiere of an Australian opera — culturally alive and historically resonant.*

### 11. 🧠 Gentle Thinkers — Intellectual Dialogue Meetup
- **Date:** Check meetup.com/gentle-thinkers for this week's session
- **Venue:** Various Brisbane CBD/inner-city venues (check group page)
- **Cost:** Free
- **Category:** Social / Meetup
- **Source:** meetup.com
- **URL:** https://www.meetup.com/gentle-thinkers/

The Gentle Thinkers is a Brisbane meetup group for those interested in intellectual conversation, learning and sharing — topics include scientific, social and political issues, with each meetup focused on one topic and everyone given the opportunity to contribute. The philosophy of the group is inspired by Bertrand Russell — "Do not feel absolutely certain of anything." The group also actively promotes events like BrisScience for members to attend together.

> 💡 *Exactly the kind of recurring community with regular attendees and natural conversation. Check the page for this week's specific meeting.*

- **Cost:** Cost of meal

The Brisbane Social Geeks group hosts events including social pub nights, boardgaming meetups, philosophy groups, guided meditations, yoga, intellectual discussions, group walking, and more. The "Dining Philosophers" is a geek term in computer science illustrating synchronization issues — the event involves a booked table for intellectual conversation and international cuisine. There's also a combined meetup with Brisbane Stoics: "An unexamined life is not worth living" (Socrates).

> 💡 *Perfect for intellectually curious, socially open people. Check the Meetup page for whether the Dining Philosophers or Brisbane Stoics sessions fall this week.*

Free volunteer guided walks at Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha are run by guides who have a love for the gardens and a desire to share their passion — walking tours for individuals and small groups (up to ten people) are free and don't require booking. Meet at the City Botanic Gardens Information Kiosk, next to the Queensland University of Technology's Main Drive pathway.

> 💡 *Low-key, free, nature-social. Great for a midweek outdoor reset with curious people.*
